messages:
olivia: quick update — I ran an occupancy + smem sweep on the A100 family for the kernel picker autotuner. trying to capture why our seqlen-dependent path chooses the smaller tile and then reg-spills at higher seq_len. results below.

devin: nice. high level summary first? :eyes:

olivia: tl;dr: small-tile path (tile_w=32, tile_h=32) helps for seq_len<=256 and batch<=4 (lower latency, better warp utilization). but for seq_len>=512 we see increased register pressure -> local store spills -> overall throughput drops ~12-18% vs medium tile (64x32). this causes the kernel selector to fallback oddly under mixed workloads.

srinivas: are we seeing more live registers per thread or just worse allocator behavior?

olivia: both. nvcc reports ~56 regs/thread for the small-tile kernel vs ~44 for the medium-tile variant. spilling shows up in `localLoad` and we see ~1.6x more memory ops in the hot loop. paste of the critical lines from the profiler: 
```
# nvprof snippet (abridged)
gpu__local_loads: 1.6e9  (small-tile)
gpu__local_loads: 1.0e9  (med-tile)
registers_per_thread: 56 (small)
registers_per_thread: 44 (med)
warp_occupancy: 0.50 (small)
warp_occupancy: 0.67 (med)
```

devin: that explains it. What about warp specialization (warp_split=true) — did you try it?

olivia: yes. warp-specialized kernel gives a ~10% latency win for batch=1, seq_len<=128. but it exacerbates reg usage for the small tile on A100 because we duplicate some per-warp scratch and scheduler occupancy drops. For batch>=8 the specialized path actually loses to the medium tile.

srinivas: interesting. So the picker should consider (seq_len, batch_size, reg_pressure) jointly. maybe we need a quick cost model: estimated_tokens/s = kernel_peak * occupancy * (1 - spill_penalty). we can estimate spill_penalty from registers_per_thread > threshold.

olivia: agreed. I propose 2 immediate changes: 1) update autotuner sample budget to include a reg_spill metric (detect via `local_loads` ratio) and penalize candidates with >1.2x local_loads relative to baseline; 2) add a seq_len routing rule: if seq_len >= 512 prefer medium_tile unless batch<=2 and measured latency for small_tile < medium_tile by >8%.

devin: sounds reasonable. can you add the autotuner patch and a fallback policy? I can wire the selector rule.

olivia: putting a draft config below (for autotuner): 
```
{
  "candidates": ["tile_32x32", "tile_64x32", "tile_128x16"],
  "metrics": ["throughput", "latency_p50", "local_loads", "registers_per_thread"],
  "penalty_rules": {
    "reg_spill_ratio": {"threshold": 1.2, "penalty": 0.15}
  },
  "seqlen_routing": [
    {"min_seq": 0, "max_seq": 255, "prefer": "tile_32x32"},
    {"min_seq": 256, "max_seq": 1023, "prefer": "tile_64x32"}
  ]
}
```

srinivas: will prototype the reg_spill detector in the autotuner harness. quick Q: do we want architecture-specific thresholds? e.g., A100 vs H100 regs/SM differ.

olivia: yes, make thresholds per device_family. for H100 we already have more regs/SM so threshold can be 1.4 instead of 1.2. add device_family to the tuning metadata.

perfbot: perf-regression detected: commit abc1234 changed default tile from 64x32 -> 32x32 for small-path. marked issue PERF-948 and tagged owners olivia, devin.

ci-deploy-bot: ran perf smoke on canary — medium_tile throughput +0.8% vs baseline, small_tile -2.1% on mixed seqlen test.

olivia: next steps: (1) update autotuner to record local_loads and registers_per_thread, (2) add per-family spill thresholds, (3) add seqlen-based picker rules and canary rollout, (4) run 24h mixed workload sweep and post results. I'll open the autotor PR and link here.

devin: ack — I'll handle the selector rule and fallback policy. thanks for the data. :thumbsup:

srinivas: ack, will start on detector.

olivia: leaving this thread open for results, will post PR links and 24h logs when ready.
